articles.headline: NFL Week 6: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday's games
articles.description: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 6.
articles.headlineJa: NFL第6週：日曜日の試合から得られた大きな収穫、疑問点、そしてファンタジー視点での考察
articles.descriptionJa: NFL Nationの記者たちが、日曜日の各試合から生じた最大の疑問に答えながら、全ての展開に反応します。第6週から得られた知見がこちらです。
articles.body:
The Sunday slate for Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season kicked off in London with a thrilling matchup between the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars. 

Wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. made his much-anticipated Texans debut, but it was quarterback C.J. Stroud who was the star of this day as Houston was able to hold off the Jaguars in a thriller.

Our NFL Nation reporters reacted to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know for teams that played Sunday. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup.

Let's get to it with the biggest lessons from Sunday.

Jump to:

HOU-JAX

Catch up on Thursday's game:

SEA-DEN

Houston 34, Jacksonville 31

Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Texans

Can quarterback C.J. Stroud keep this hot start going? Even though Stroud did have an ill-timed interception that gave the Jaguars a chance late in the fourth quarter, he was stellar. The fourth-year quarterback is continuing to perform at an MVP level, but against the Jaguars, Houston needed him at his best -- and he delivered. He led the game-winning drive to cap a 306-yard, three-touchdown outing in his first London performance.

Trend to watch: The Texans' "elite" defense has been far from it. Coach DeMeco Ryans took over playcalling this week, but his unit allowed 31 points. It's the third time this season that the Texans have allowed at least 30 points. -- DJ Bien-Aime

Next game: vs. Giants (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Jaguars

Is it time for the Jaguars to fully unleash Travis Hunter on offense? They may need to. Hunter had his best offensive game of the season. He caught four passes for 59 yards and a touchdown after having just two catches for 17 yards in the first five games. The Jaguars needed him to step up because receiver Brian Thomas Jr. struggled, dropping two passes -- including one that would have given the Jaguars a chance to attempt a long field goal at the end of the first half. Thomas, who had an issue with drops last year, didn't play an offensive snap in the second half after playing 15 in the first. Hunter, with a bigger offensive workload, could make up for Thomas' struggles.

Trend to watch: The Jaguars are banged up at safety, with Antonio Johnson leaving the game with an ankle injury. They were already down Caleb Ransaw (IR) and went to Kaevon Merriweather, who was on the practice squad until he was signed to the active roster before last week's game. With the bye next week, the Jaguars need to get healthy and possibly make another move depending on how long Johnson is out. -- Michael DiRocco

Next game: vs. Colts (Nov. 1, 1 p.m. ET)

articles.headline: Panthers' Tremble admits TD taunt was payback for 'suplex' by Eagles' DeJean
articles.description: Panthers tight end Tommy Tremble apologized for costing his team a penalty after he taunted defensive back Cooper DeJean, saying it was retaliation for an earlier personal foul.
articles.headlineJa: パンサーズのトレムブル、TD後の挑発はイーグルスのディージャンによる「スーズレックス」への仕返しだったと認める
articles.descriptionJa: パンサーズのタイトエンド、トミー・トレムブルは、ディフェンシブバックのクーパー・ディージャンを挑発してチームにペナルティを与えてしまったことを謝罪。これは、以前行われたパーソナルファウルに対する報復だったと語った。
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- Carolina Panthers tight end Tommy Tremble added some spice to his game-sealing touchdown catch in the fourth quarter of Sunday's 25-14 win over the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field.

After breaking free from coverage, a wide-open Tremble snagged a 19-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Bryce Young. After the score, Tremble immediately pointed at All-Pro defensive back Cooper DeJean, who was trying to catch up to the ball. Tremble was flagged for taunting, which set up a 48-yard extra point attempt, which was missed -- wide right -- by second-year kicker Ryan Fitzgerald.

After the game, Tremble acknowledged the finger wagging at DeJean was retaliation for an earlier personal foul by the defensive back. On the previous play, DeJean was penalized for unnecessary roughness on Tremble's fellow tight end, Mitchell Evans.

"It happens -- it's football, tempers get up and stuff like that," Tremble said. "And so, it was kind of not that cool for him to do that to Mitch. And so, in the heat of the moment, stuff happens and I'll be paying that fine, probably, next week."

DeJean and Evans got tangled up on a 5-yard run by running back Chuba Hubbard. Following the play, DeJean and Evans got into a brief skirmish that caused Evans to leave his feet and fall to the ground hard.

After the fall, Evans limped to the huddle and the Panthers were awarded 15 yards.

 

"The dude was just on my back," DeJean said. "He was trying to put me to the ground and was trying to walk over me as I was still standing up. Obviously I didn't want him to do that so I stood up, he flipped over top of me. [The explanation I got] was that I picked him up and slammed him to the ground.

"It's pretty tough to do when your arms are in front of you on the ground and he's on your back, to pick someone up and slam them to the ground. I don't know. I guess I just can't put myself in that position."

Evans laughed off the incident in the locker room after the win. But he said he started to cramp as he left his feet.

"I don't know what happened," Evans said. "And then I just started cramping like mid-flip, mid-suplex [laughs] and landed on my back. I was like, 'Oh, that did not feel good.' But it got us 15 [penalty yards] ... so I'll take it."

Tremble said he didn't see what caused the penalty on DeJean initially. But once he heard Evans go down after the play, he was irked for his teammate.

"I just thought that personal foul was kind of egregious," Tremble said. "It was uncalled for -- something that didn't need to happen. I shouldn't have retaliated. That wasn't cool of me to do."

Tremble caught four passes for 46 yards and both of the Panthers' Week 6 touchdowns Sunday. He was also used as a versatile option, as he lined up all around the field, including fullback.

articles.headline: Stephen Curry limps out of practice after tweaking right knee
articles.description: Stephen Curry left the Warriors' open practice in San Francisco on Sunday night after appearing to tweak his right knee on a perimeter move.
articles.headlineJa: ステフィン・カリー、右膝を痛め足を引きずりながら練習を離脱
articles.descriptionJa: ステフィン・カリーは日曜夜、サンフランシスコで行われたウォリアーズの公開練習中、ペリメーターでの動きで右膝を痛めた様子を見せ、練習を後にした。
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors superstar guard Stephen Curry left the team's open practice in San Francisco on Sunday night, limping to the locker room after appearing to tweak his right knee on a perimeter move.

Curry was lined up against reserve guard De'Anthony Melton on the wing when he showed frustration after a misstep, banging the basketball on the floor. Action stopped and Curry's teammates expressed immediate concern at his discomfort.

 

There was no immediate update from the Warriors.

This is the same knee that caused Curry major trouble last season, forcing him to miss 27 games the final two months while dealing with what the team deemed "runner's knee."

Curry returned for the final few games, but spent his summer attempting to get his knee and body right for training camp. He received the full green light for practice, but Warriors coach Steve Kerr has been clear they intended to ramp Curry up slowly for the season, protecting the knee.

Curry will turn 39 in March. The Warriors open the season Wednesday night in Los Angeles against the Lakers.

articles.headline: McCarthy nearly rallies Giants after Winston benched; Skattebo logs no carries
articles.description: Giants coach John Harbaugh said Sunday he's not ready to name a starting quarterback for Week 7 after J.J. McCarthy replaced Jameis Winston against the Saints.
articles.headlineJa: ウィンストンがベンチに下げられた後、マッカーシーがジャイアンツを逆転寸前まで押し上げるも、スカッテボのラン回数はゼロ
articles.descriptionJa: ジャイアンツのジョン・ハーボー監督は日曜、セインツ戦でジェイ・ジェイ・マッカーシーがジェイミス・ウィンストンに代わって出場した後、第7週の先発クォーターバックを決定する準備はまだできていないと語った。
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- The New York Giants have serious questions on offense after a 37-24 loss to the New Orleans Saints. Coach John Harbaugh was unable to answer a question immediately after the game about who starts at quarterback next week against the Houston Texans and running back Cam Skattebo also saw his playing time slashed following a string of fumbles.

Harbaugh has to choose between Jameis Winston and J.J. McCarthy at quarterback. McCarthy came in early in the fourth quarter and almost led a miraculous comeback while throwing for 243 yards. Winston, meanwhile, lost for the first time in four starts on Sunday as he threw a pair of interceptions before being removed.

"Can't answer that now," Harbaugh said in his postgame news conference about his starting quarterback moving forward. "Game just ended 10 minutes ago."

McCarthy, a former first-round pick of the Minnesota Vikings who was acquired in a trade by the Giants late last month, led three scoring drives and got the Giants inside the red zone in the final seconds. But his fourth-down pass with under 20 seconds remaining sailed over the head of triple-covered tight end Isaiah Likely in the back of the end zone.

McCarthy finished 11-of-21 for 243 yards with a touchdown and interception. He also led the Giants with 26 rushing yards to seemingly open the door for a potential quarterback change.

"Like I said, I can't answer it now. It's not even up for discussion or conversation right now," Harbaugh said. "We got to go back and go to work. I have no problem with Jameis whatsoever. I love the way he competes. I love the way he fights. All those kinds of things. Play was up and down today for sure. But all those things will be decided [and] not 10 minutes after the game."

The 243 yards was the second-most passing yards in a fourth quarter by a quarterback who didn't start over the past 25 seasons, according to ESPN Research. Only Sage Rosenfels (249) had more in Week 7 of 2007 for the Tennessee Titans.

McCarthy wasn't overly impressed because the Giants still lost the game. He's also not thinking about whether he did enough to wrestle the job from Winston.

"The only thing I'm focused on is getting better each and every day," McCarthy said. "At the end of the day, Coach Harbaugh has to make a lot of decisions. Those are his decisions. I trust him wholeheartedly with any decision he makes."

Winston became the Giants' starter when Jaxson Dart was lost for the season in Week 2 with a knee injury. He won his first two starts before last week's tie with the Washington Commanders.

The veteran backup finished 14 of 26 passing for 152 yards with one touchdown pass and two interceptions against the Saints. He knows it's up to Harbaugh whether he remains the starter.

articles.headline: Cardinals beat Rams 18-16 on Chad Ryland's 6th field goal as time expires
articles.description: — Chad Ryland kicked his sixth field goal a 43-yarder as time expired, and the Arizona Cardinals rallied for a stunning 18-16 victory over the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday.
articles.headlineJa: チャド・ライランドの6本目のフィールドゴールが試合終了間際に決まり、カーディナルズがラムズに18-16で勝利
articles.descriptionJa: チャド・ライランドが試合終了間際に43ヤードの6本目のフィールドゴールを成功させ、アリゾナ・カーディナルズは日曜、ロサンゼルス・ラムズを相手に18-16という劇的な逆転勝利を収めた。
articles.body:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- — Chad Ryland kicked his sixth field goal a 43-yarder as time expired, and the Arizona Cardinals rallied for a stunning 18-16 victory over the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday.


              Punter Ethan Evans kicked a go-ahead extra point after Colby Parkinson caught a touchdown pass from Matthew Stafford with 47 seconds to play for the vaunted Rams (2-4), who struggled all day before mounting a desperate final scoring drive.


              But the Cardinals immediately moved 36 yards into field goal range on Jalen Brooks' long reception and an unnecessary roughness penalty on Josh Wallace. Three snaps later, Ryland buried his final kick to seal a shocking upset for Arizona (2-4), a double-digit underdog.


              Jacoby Brissett passed for 218 yards to balance a superb defensive game by the Cardinals against the preseason Super Bowl favorites. New Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur won his first meeting with former boss Sean McVay and earned Arizona's second win this season at SoFi Stadium, where it also beat the Chargers in Week 1.


              Matthew Stafford passed for 222 yards and two scores for the Rams (2-4), who are in complete disarray after three losses in their last four games, including this setback at home to a team McVay had beaten 16 times in 19 meetings. Los Angeles still rallied, and Evans even came through with his first career placekick after new Rams kicker Blake Grupe injured his knee making a tackle in the first quarter — but Ryland and the Cardinals cashed in their final chance.


              Stafford hit Blake Corum for the game’s first touchdown in a dismal offensive performance by the Rams, who came in leading the NFL in total offense. Although being forced to play without a kicking game didn’t help, the Rams struggled to move the ball all day, and they turned it over twice in Cardinals territory in the fourth quarter.


              Arizona’s defense had been one of the NFL’s worst this season until it held McVay, Stafford and their talented unit to 286 yards. All-Pro receiver Puka Nacua had half of his six receptions on the final drive.


              LaFleur was McVay's offensive coordinator for the previous three seasons. He is the eighth of McVay's former assistants to become an NFL head coach.


              Grupe hit a 44-yard field goal in the first quarter, but the newcomer injured his knee when he was forced to make a downfield tackle on the ensuing kickoff in the Rams’ latest special teams nightmare.


              Ryland's fourth field goal put the Cardinals ahead 12-9 in the third quarter. After Ryland's fifth field goal, Cody Simon forced a fumble by Rams tight end Tyler Higbee deep in Cards territory with 7:47 to play. Los Angeles' defense quickly got the ball back, but the offense turned it over on downs.


              The Rams got one last chance from their 15 with 2:48 to play, and Stafford stepped up in the pocket to find Nacua for a rambling 42-yard gain.

articles.headline: Aaron Rodgers' 2026 NFL season: Tracking records, milestones
articles.description: The Steelers QB is chasing records in his 22nd NFL season, and ESPN is chronicling his "last rodeo."
articles.headlineJa: アーロン・ロジャースの2026年NFLシーズン：記録とマイルストーンを追跡
articles.descriptionJa: NFLでの22シーズン目を迎えるスチールのQBは記録に挑んでおり、ESPNはその「最後の舞台」を記録している。
articles.body:
Entering his 22nd NFL season -- or as Aaron Rodgers says, "his last rodeo" -- the 42-year-old Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback is on the cusp of joining several exclusive clubs as he moves up the ranks in the league record books.

In 2025, he passed former teammate Brett Favre to take sole possession of fourth place in career touchdown passes thrown with his 509th TD pass in the Week 3 win against the New England Patriots.

"Every now and then I made some special throws that led to touchdowns, but I've been playing a long time, and it's a longevity thing," Rodgers said before passing Favre's mark last season. "I'm proud of it, but not a big deal."

Rodgers supplanted Ben Roethlisberger for fifth in all-time passing yards in a loss to the Cincinnati Bengals on Oct. 16, 2025. But now, Rodgers is closing in on his final opportunities to add to that growing list of historic accomplishments.

Among the milestones in reach for Rodgers are becoming the fourth quarterback in NFL history to appear in 300 games (as of Week 6 he has appeared in 293), joining Tom Brady (383), Favre (326) and Drew Brees (305), throwing the fourth-most touchdown passes in NFL history (as of Week 6, he has 539) and having the second-most regular-season games with multiple touchdown passes. And after Week 6, he needs 2,239 yards to become the fifth player to reach 70,000 passing yards. 

This season, we're chronicling Rodgers' individual milestones week by week as he rides his last rodeo. Follow along here for the weekly installments.

Preseason: 0-for-0, 0 yards, 0 INT, 0 sacks, 0 rushes

Despite early hints that Rodgers would take the field during the Steelers' first preseason under McCarthy, the veteran quarterback instead spent two games on the sideline and one on his couch at home. With Rodgers' top two receivers in DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr. sidelined with preseason injuries, McCarthy opted to also keep his quarterback under wraps.

Rodgers isn't a stranger to sitting out the preseason in recent years. He didn't play in any preseason games for the Steelers in 2025, nor for the New York Jets in 2024 following his season-ending left Achilles tear in Week 1 of the 2023 season.

Week 1: Steelers 20, Falcons 13

Rodgers' stat line: 221 yards, 1 TD, 0 INTs, 2 sacks, 3 rushes for -1 yard

Rodgers didn't break any records this week, but he pulled within one touchdown pass of Peyton Manning for fourth most in NFL history with his second-quarter throw to tight end Pat Freiermuth for 6 yards. The touchdown toss was Rodgers' 232nd of the regular season. Rodgers had 26 pass attempts in the first half, his most attempts in the first half of a game since 2020 at Minnesota as a member of the Green Bay Packers, per ESPN Research.

After Sunday's game, coach Mike McCarthy said he wanted to find more balance in his offense, which ran the ball just 21 times to Rodgers' 40 pass attempts. Rodgers, though, didn't mind all the throwing.

articles.headline: Sources: Kings guard Ben Simmons believed to have torn Achilles tendon
articles.description: Sacramento Kings guard Ben Simmons, a three-time All-Star who agreed to a one-year, $3.5 million contract on Sept. 4, is believed to have sustained a torn Achilles tendon after receiving a preliminary diagnosis on the injury, sources told ESPN on Sunday.
articles.headlineJa: 関係者：キングスのガード、ベン・シモンズがアキレス腱断裂の可能性
articles.descriptionJa: サクラメント・キングスのガードで、9月4日に1年350万ドルの契約に合意した3度のオールスター選出経験を持つベン・シモンズが、負傷の予備診断の結果、アキレス腱を断裂したとみられると関係者が日曜日にESPNに語った。
articles.body:
Sacramento Kings guard Ben Simmons is believed to have sustained a torn Achilles tendon after receiving a preliminary diagnosis on the injury from the team, sources told ESPN on Sunday.

This signifies a suspected season-ending injury for Simmons after rejuvenated and impressive training camp and preseason performances.

A three-time All-Star, Simmons agreed to a one-year, $3.5 million contract with the Kings on Sept. 4. Healthy at the time of the deal, the 6-foot-10, 240-pound guard impressed Kings general manager Scott Perry when he worked out for him in Miami and had an hourlong meeting in late August.

Simmons also traveled to Sacramento to visit the Kings and impressed coach Doug Christie and other members of the basketball staff at the team's practice facility last month where he underwent an in-depth medical exam and conducted an on-court workout.

In the following days, the Kings offered Simmons a contract with the expectation of him being a backup point guard for rookie Darius Acuff Jr. and play positions 1 through 5. For the Kings, Simmons was to serve as a high-upside reclamation project who still has years left in his perspective prime.

Simmons played two preseason games for the Kings, averaging 10.5 points in 17.5 minutes.

articles.headline: Week 6 winners and losers: Lawrence, Nabers impress; Robinson, Henry disappoint
articles.description: Malik Nabers, Trevor Lawrence and Tyler Shough came up big in Week 6, while Bijan Robinson and Derrick Henry underwhelmed.
articles.headlineJa: 第6週の勝者と敗者：ローレンスとネイバーズが躍動、ロビンソンとヘンリーは期待外れ
articles.descriptionJa: 第6週ではマリク・ネイバーズ、トレバー・ローレンス、タイラー・シャフが大きな活躍を見せた一方、ビジャン・ロビンソンとデリック・ヘンリーは精彩を欠いた。
articles.body:
Week 6 of the 2026 fantasy football season featured big games by Malik Nabers, Trevor Lawrence and Tyler Shough. On the flip side, Bijan Robinson and Derrick Henry had disappointing outings.

Who were the big winners and losers around the league during the sixth week of the fantasy football season?

Matt Bowen and Tristan H. Cockcroft offer their analysis.

Jump to a topic:

Ranking winners | Ranking losers 

Biggest injuries and what's next

Ranking fantasy winners of Week 6

1. Malik Nabers, WR, New York Giants

Nabers scored 28.5 points in the Week 6 loss to the Saints, catching 12 of 15 targets (from multiple quarterbacks), finishing with 165 receiving yards. This is Nabers' third straight game with 23 or more fantasy points, and he has seen 35 targets over his past two. After J.J. McCarthy replaced Jameis Winston under center Sunday, the Giants could make a switch at quarterback heading into Week 7. But I don't see how that impacts Nabers heading into the matchup versus a Houston defense that has been surprisingly poor against wide receivers this season. Keep Nabers as a WR1. -- Bowen

2. Trevor Lawrence, QB, and Bhayshul Tuten, RB, Jacksonville Jaguars

Tuten and the Jaguars' running game couldn't get much done on the ground against a tough Houston Texans defense, but he caught a pair of receiving touchdowns and nearly had a third when he was pushed out of bounds at the 1-yard line on an 11-yard catch. Lawrence, meanwhile, has scored 20-plus fantasy points in back-to-back games in London, totaling 27.34 despite a 58.5% completion rate. The Jaguars' offense didn't have its best game in Week 6 -- and individually, Lawrence was picked in the end zone, while Chris Rodriguez Jr. had superior rushing metrics to Tuten -- but it seems sound on the whole. Heading into the bye, Lawrence is a clear fantasy QB1 while Tuten is a somewhat matchup-dependent RB2. -- Cockcroft

3. Germie Bernard, WR, Pittsburgh Steelers

Bernard has emerged as a viable weekly fantasy starter in the injury absences of Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger), both placed on IR over the past eight days, piling up yards after the catch as a short-range target for Aaron Rodgers. Bernard scored 25.7 fantasy points on 12 targets, including catching the winning touchdown in overtime. Best yet, he gets great matchups over the next two weeks (@NO, CLE). -- Cockcroft

4. Tyler Shough, QB, New Orleans Saints

After a brutal Week 5 game versus the Vikings (minus-0.16 points), Shough bounced back in Sunday's win over the Giants, scoring a season-best 26.96 points. Shough finished with only 144 passing yards, but he threw three touchdown passes and rushed for 33 yards and a score on five carries. Shough has now topped the 22-point mark in four of six games played this season. He'll remain in the QB2 range for the Week 7 matchup against a Steelers defense ranking in the top five versus quarterbacks. -- Bowen

articles.headline: NBA preseason buzz: Latest on trades, news and intel
articles.description: The NBA regular season is less than a week away, and we're tracking all the news, deals, and trades across the league.
articles.headlineJa: NBAプレシーズン・バズ：トレード、ニュース、最新情報のまとめ
articles.descriptionJa: NBAレギュラーシーズン開幕まで1週間を切った今、リーグ全体のあらゆるニュース、契約、トレードを追っている。
articles.body:
With the preseason games coming to a close soon, the 2026-27 NBA season is less than a week away from tipping off.

How will LeBron James and Jaylen Brown look on the court in their new Philadelphia 76ers uniforms? What will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first season away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their impact this season?

Check back here for all the latest buzz, news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders, with the latest info at the top:

Quick links:

Free agency grades | Trade grades

Trade tracker | Transactions | Offseason buzz

Depth charts | Trade machine | More

Oct. 18

Suns' Ighodaro signs multi-year deal to stay in Phoenix

Phoenix Suns center Oso Ighodaro has agreed to a three-year, $29 million contract extension through the 2030-31 season, his agent Erika Ruiz of Primera Sports told ESPN.

The Suns will pick up Ighodaro's $2.5M team option for 2027-28, so the extension starts in 2028 and runs through 2031 for the franchise's 2024 second-round pick.

Simmons tears Achilles, out for the season

Sacramento Kings guard Ben Simmons tore an Achilles tendon at practice Sunday, sources told ESPN. Simmons, the 2016 No. 1 pick whom the Kings signed this offseason, was readying to play his first regular-season game since 2024-2025.

Oct. 16

Marks: A busy weekend of transaction expected

The last weekend of the offseason is expected to bring a flurry of transactions.

Starting on Saturday Oct. 17, teams will need to decide on players signed to non-guaranteed contracts. If a player is on the roster past 5 p.m. ET, teams will begin incurring a per day salary charge.

For example, the New York Knicks would be charged $17,622 per day against the cap if James Wiseman is not waived by Saturday. However, despite a mandate to remain under the second apron, New York is allowed to keep Wiseman and Bruce Brown to start the season.

The deadline for rookie extensions is Monday by 6 p.m. ET.

Since the start of the offseason, five players -- Victor Wembanyama, Amen and Ausar Thompson, Keyonte George and Brandin Podziemski -- have signed rookie extensions. The 2023 rookie class of extended players are below the per year average of 11 players we have seen since 2023.

Some of the notable names to watch include Brandon Miller and Cason Wallace. Keep in mind that out of the 34 players who signed rookie extensions in the prior three seasons, 17 came on the last day of eligibility.

The rookie extension deadline is not the only date teams are paying attention to, however. Oct. 19 is also the deadline to extend veterans who have two years left on their contract -- not including an option year -- and the last day to reduce rosters to 15 players on standard contracts. -- Bobby Marks

articles.headline: Mou doesn't understand 'obsession' with elbow from Madrid's Güler
articles.description: José Mourinho claimed he hadn't seen "images" of an elbow by Arda Güler -- which saw no intervention from the referee -- in Real Madrid's 4-1 win over Sevilla.
articles.headlineJa: モウリーニョ、マドリードのギュレルによるエルボーへの『執着』を理解できず
articles.descriptionJa: ジョゼ・モウリーニョは、レアル・マドリードがセビージャに4-1で勝利した試合において、審判の介入もなかったアルダ・ギュレルによるエルボーの「映像」は見ていないと主張した。
articles.body:
José Mourinho claimed he hadn't seen "any images" of an alleged elbow from Arda Güler -- which saw no intervention from the referee -- in Real Madrid's 4-1 win over Sevilla on Sunday, saying he didn't understand the "obsession" with the incident in his postmatch news conference.

Sevilla coach Luis Garcia Plaza was furious at the decision not to send off Güler for the first-half clash with Gerard 'Peque' Fernandez -- which occurred with the game tied at 0-0 -- saying his team was "denied the chance to play another game, 11 against 10."

However Mourinho suggested the discussion was an attempt by his counterpart to divert attention from the eventual 4-1 scoreline, after goals from Güler, Kylian Mbappé and Yan Diomande left Madrid six points behind leaders Barcelona heading into next weekend's Clásico.

"Nobody has been able to show me what they say happened," Mourinho said. "There aren't any images. I've asked for TV images, and for images from my staff who have the tactical camera, and I haven't been able to see any image of what's being talked about, what annoyed Luis [Garcia Plaza].

"Honestly, if one day something happens that benefits us, I'll have no problem in saying it. But I think the opposite will happen many more times, that's the tendency. I haven't seen anything. Until Saturday, if someone gets a clear and objective image to me of something I haven't seen -- and which my player says didn't happen -- I'll be there [to talk about it], but until then, nothing."

"Today we should have played with an extra man, from the 25th minute, 11 against 10," Garcia Plaza insisted. "I don't want to talk about the game after that. It's incredible. I saw it. Peque at halftime was saying 'he hit me.' It's a red card.

"Maybe we wouldn't have won, but we should have been playing 11 against 10, for 65 minutes. That's the summary of the game."

Madrid's victory at the Bernabéu allowed them to go into an important week -- with a Champions League game with RB Leipzig followed by the Clásico at Camp Nou -- with a run of three consecutive wins since the international break.

Mourinho made a number of key decisions in his team selection, bringing Güler into central midfield and starting Endrick after both impressed at Roma in midweek.

"I understand Luis [Garcia Plaza], with a team that loses 4-1," Mourinho said. "If the coach gets four or five questions about something which hasn't happened, that's fantastic for him.

"When it happened, I told [Real Madrid assistant coach] Pedro [Machado] I wanted to see it, but I couldn't see anything. Maybe there are other cameras, but until now, nothing."

"Have any of you seen it clearly?" Mourinho asked journalists. "That's why I don't understand the obsession with asking about it."

Mourinho said he also hadn't watched rivals Barcelona's 5-2 win at Real Betis a day earlier, which included a stunning Giovani Lo Celso goal for Betis being disallowed for an earlier handball.

articles.headline: Roberto De Zerbi on latest Tottenham training ploy: 'We removed phones' from meals
articles.description: Roberto De Zerbi has revealed phones were banned from meals during Tottenham's warm weather training camp in Marbella in his latest attempt to turn a vastly-assembled squad into a team.
articles.body:
Roberto De Zerbi has revealed phones were banned from meals during Tottenham's warm weather training camp in Marbella in his latest attempt to turn a vastly-assembled squad into a team.

Spurs committed more than £380 million ($505m) on new signings this summer with 10 players joining, but they will start Monday's home fixture with Coventry at the bottom of the Premier League with no wins from their opening six fixtures.

De Zerbi knows pressure will build if Tottenham fail to win, but will hope a midweek excursion to Spain can help turn frowns upside down in N17.

"We worked on the pitch, we stayed together -- we removed phones from breakfast, lunch and dinner to stay together because now it is like [phone] all the time," De Zerbi told a press conference.

"We had two or three important meetings speaking about football, our situation and how everyone has to take responsibility. And nothing more. There were some dinners just for the players, some dinners just for the staff.

"As a coach you understand you have to improve, you have to change the situation and you try to find all solutions.

"I already did this type of training camp two times with Marseille and it was a good solution. I spoke with the club, with Vinai [Venkatesham], with Johan [Lange], with the owner and together we took the decision, but it's nothing special.

"It's just to spend more time together because in pre-season we couldn't. We had many new players and players who came back from the World Cup. Three or four days together without family, putting the club at the top of their priorities, is normal and is good."

Asked if players were able to go out independently in Marbella, De Zerbi said: "Yes, with freedom. With no military rules. I love freedom."

Fit-again Dejan Kulusevski was part of the Tottenham squad in Spain along with James Maddison, who should face old club Coventry but is yet to start for Spurs since he damaged anterior cruciate ligaments in 2025 and Xavi Simons remains absent with the same injury.

"I am very close with Xavi Simons for example in this moment. I follow him step by step in his journey as an injured player. Like Maddison, because the management of Maddison is totally different. He is another special player and now is available to play," De Zerbi said.

- Kulusevski set to return to Tottenham squad after 526-day injury absence

"Kulusevski was a very important player, even last season when he was injured. It is a part of this job for the players, but at the same time can be a crucial moment to become better, to become stronger.

"You need to play many games to reach the best physical condition but there are players able to be important, even if they play 10, 15 or 20 minutes and James is one player like this.

"Right now he is ready to start the game, but I don't know if we will start with him. I'm waiting for that moment."

articles.headline: Yan Diomande, Kylian Mbappé lead Real Madrid rout of Sevilla
articles.description: Kylian Mbappé's brilliant double on Sunday helped Real Madrid prepare for next week's El Clasico with a 4-1 triumph over Sevilla at the Bernabeu.
articles.headlineJa: ヤン・ディオマンデとキリアン・エムバペが主導し、レアル・マドリードがセビージャを圧倒
articles.descriptionJa: 日曜日にキリアン・エムバペが鮮やかな2ゴールを決め、レアル・マドリードはベルナベウでセビージャに4-1で勝利し、来週のエル・クラシコに向けて弾みをつけた。
articles.body:
Kylian Mbappé's brilliant double on Sunday helped Real Madrid prepare for next week's El Clasico with a 4-1 triumph over Sevilla at the Bernabeu.

The France striker finished off a fine team move in style to double Madrid's lead in the 37th minute after Arda Güler put the hosts ahead with a curling strike on the half hour.

Mbappé extended their advantage with a Panenka penalty after the break and although Manu Bueno scored a consolation goal, Yan Diomande soon fired home to wrap up the three points.

Victory comes just days after earning a stunning 4-3 comeback win over Jose Mourinho's former club Roma in the Champions League and ahead of a huge week for Los Blancos.

They return to European action against RB Leipzig on Wednesday before Sunday's trip to the Spotify Camp Nou, where Madrid take on LaLiga leaders Barcelona, who have started the domestic season with nine straight wins.

Madrid pulled off the one-sided win without the services of Vinícius Júnior, who is serving the first of a four-game ban for pulling the hair of Villarreal's Nathan Saliba last weekend.

Information from PA was used in this recap.

articles.headline: Knicks waive Bruce Brown, keep James Wiseman ahead of opener
articles.description: The Knicks are waiving Bruce Brown and keeping James Wiseman on the roster as the team heads into its regular-season opener, sources told ESPN.
articles.headlineJa: ニックス、ブルース・ブラウンを放出、ジェームズ・ウィズマンは開幕に向けて残留
articles.descriptionJa: ESPNが報じたところによると、ニックスはレギュラーシーズン開幕を控え、ブルース・ブラウンを放出する一方で、ジェームズ・ウィズマンをロスターに留めることを決定した。
articles.body:
The New York Knicks waived Bruce Brown and will keep James Wiseman on the roster as the team heads into its regular-season opener.

Brown was one of several players on non-guaranteed deals vying for one of New York's final two available roster spots. Tony Bradley, Ochai Agbaji and Drew Eubanks were all also waived in recent days.

Wiseman appeared in all four of the Knicks' preseason games and impressed in 24 minutes vs. the Toronto Raptors on Tuesday, when he scored 18 points and grabbed 10 rebounds.

 

According to ESPN's Bobby Marks, the Knicks could have kept Brown and Wiseman, but because they are only $3.2 million below their self-imposed hard cap at the second apron, retaining both players would've been difficult.  

Wiseman, 25, will join Karl-Anthony Towns and Andre Drummond in New York's center rotation. The reigning NBA champions lost key reserve big man Mitchell Robinson to the Boston Celtics this past summer via free agency.

The Knicks begin the NBA's regular season Tuesday, when they host the new-look Philadelphia 76ers.

articles.headline: 76ers, needing frontcourt help, convert 7-foot-6 Tacko Fall to two-way contract
articles.description: The 76ers, dealing with injuries in the frontcourt, have converted center Tacko Fall to a two-way contract.
articles.headlineJa: フロントコートの補強を必要とする76ers、7フィート6インチのタコ・フォールとツーウェイ契約を締結
articles.descriptionJa: フロントコートでの怪我に悩まされている76ersは、センターのタコ・フォールをツーウェイ契約に切り替えた。
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- The 76ers have converted center Tacko Fall to a two-way contract, the team announced Saturday.

Last month, the Sixers signed the 7-foot-6 center to an Exhibit 10 deal, and injuries to the frontcourt likely led to Fall getting this spot.

Ariel Hukporti, projected to be the Sixers' backup center, suffered a season-ending right Achilles tear in the preseason. Center Adem Bona, potentially the next man up, has been sidelined with a foot injury, and Dominick Barlow has battled back soreness that kept him out of the preseason.

Fall hasn't played in the NBA since the 2021-22 season, when he was with the Cleveland Cavaliers. This will be his fourth season in the NBA. He played his first two in Boston with new Sixers forward Jaylen Brown.

Fall, 30, most recently played for the Ningbo Rockets of the Chinese Basketball Association.

articles.headline: No. 1 pick AJ Dybantsa injures ankle during Wizards' preseason finale
articles.description: First overall pick AJ Dybantsa exited the Wizards' preseason finale after injuring his ankle on an awkward landing and will undergo further evaluation.
articles.headlineJa: ドラフト1位指名のAJ・ディバンツァ、ウィザーズのプレシーズン最終戦で足首を負傷
articles.descriptionJa: 全体1位指名のAJ・ディバンツァが、ウィザーズのプレシーズン最終戦で不自然な着地により足首を負傷して途中交代した。今後、詳細な検査を受ける予定。
articles.body:
First overall pick AJ Dybantsa exited the Washington Wizards' preseason finale Friday after injuring his ankle on an awkward landing and will undergo further evaluation.

Wizards coach Brian Keefe told sideline reporter Chase Hughes that Dybantsa had suffered a mild ankle sprain but that the decision to keep him out for the rest of the game was more precautionary.

"We'll look at it more when we get more information," Keefe said.

Dybantsa fell to the ground after landing on his left ankle following a midrange jump shot before limping to the locker room. He had scored 12 points in 15 minutes before his exit in the second quarter.

The Wizards open the regular season Wednesday against the Milwaukee Bucks.
